title: Category O Finiteness Duality and Blocks

items.title: The classical BGG category O
items.statement: The full category of finitely generated U(g)-modules that are h-semisimple and locally U(n+)-finite; include zero and g-linear morphisms.

items.title: Noetherianity of the enveloping algebra
items.statement: For finite-dimensional g, U(g) is left and right Noetherian.
items.proof_strategy: Lift finite homogeneous generators of gr(I) in the polynomial algebra gr U(g), subtract leading symbols and induct on degree; same proof for right ideals

items.title: Finite Borel-stable generators and weight flags
items.statement: Every O-object is generated by a finite-dimensional b-stable h-semisimple subspace E; E admits a finite b-stable flag with one-dimensional quotients annihilated by n+.
items.proof_strategy: Replace finitely many generators by their weight components and U(n+) spans; maximal weights give invariant lines and induction on dim E gives the flag

items.title: The support description of category O with finite generation
items.statement: For a finitely generated h-semisimple g-module, local n+-finiteness is equivalent to support in finitely many cones lambda_i-Q+. In either case every weight space is finite dimensional.
items.proof_strategy: Forward: PBW applied to finite E. Reverse: PBW monomials raising a fixed weight have bounded total root height in each cone, hence only finitely many monomials can act nontrivially; no finite-dimensional-weight hypothesis is needed for this direction

items.title: Verma and finite-dimensional weight modules belong to O
items.statement: Vermas, their highest-weight quotients, and finite-dimensional h-semisimple g-modules lie in O.
items.proof_strategy: Use the Verma PBW cone; finite-dimensional weight modules satisfy all three axioms directly

items.title: Category O is abelian and extension closed among weight modules
items.statement: O is closed under submodules, quotients and finite direct sums, hence abelian. If 0->M->E->N->0 has M,N in O and E h-semisimple, then E is in O. No assertion for arbitrary ambient g-module extensions.

references.title: Chen, Lecture 2 §3 Lemma 3.3 and Warning 3.4, p.5
Chen, Lecture 8 §3 Theorem 3.9 proof, p.5: extension closure in the weight-module category

items.proof_strategy: Submodule finite generation follows by the elementary finite-free-module induction over a left Noetherian ring; subquotients inherit weight decomposition. For extensions lift generators, take union of supports, and apply the qualified support equivalence. An induced rank-two Borel Jordan extension proves the middle-term weight hypothesis is essential

items.title: A nonzero O-object has a highest-weight vector
items.statement: Every nonzero O-object contains a nonzero weight vector annihilated by n+.
items.proof_strategy: Take a maximal weight above any weight in the finite union of cones; bounded height ensures termination

items.title: The simple objects of O
items.statement: Simple O-objects are exactly L(lambda), with distinct labels nonisomorphic.
items.proof_strategy: A highest-weight vector gives a nonzero Verma surjection to a simple; highest weight uniqueness distinguishes the labels

items.title: Finite filtrations by highest-weight quotients
items.statement: Every O-object has a finite filtration with nonzero factors quotient modules of Vermas; it is also a quotient of a module with a finite Verma flag.
items.proof_strategy: Induce the finite b-flag: PBW makes U(g) free as a right U(b)-module, so induction is exact. Map the resulting flag into M and delete repeated images. No truncation hypothesis or claim that M itself has a Verma flag

items.title: The center has finite-dimensional image on each O-object
items.statement: Z(U(g))/Ann_Z(M) is finite dimensional for M in O.
items.proof_strategy: Take the finite sum of full weight spaces containing chosen generators. It is Z-stable and finite dimensional; restriction embeds the image algebra in End(E), since a central element killing E kills its U(g)-span

items.title: Generalized central-character subcategories
items.statement: For m_chi=ker chi set M_chi={v: m_chi^N v=0 for some N}; O_chi consists of M with M=M_chi.

items.title: Generalized central-character summands
items.statement: Every O-object decomposes canonically as a finite sum of its M_chi; on each summand a common power of m_chi annihilates the entire module.
items.proof_strategy: Prove the elementary simultaneous generalized-eigenspace decomposition of a finite-dimensional commutative algebra in its regular representation; polynomial spectral idempotents sum to 1. Their images acting on M are g-submodules. Nilpotence of the local maximal ideal follows from finite simultaneous triangularization

items.title: Generalized central-character decomposition of O
items.statement: O is the categorical direct sum of O_chi, with finitely many nonzero components for each object; projections are exact and morphisms between distinct summands vanish.
items.proof_strategy: Central idempotents commute with maps; use a common finite image algebra for a short exact sequence to prove exactness componentwise

items.title: Finite weight-space detection of subquotients
items.statement: If M has generalized character chi_lambda, every nonzero subquotient has a nonzero weight space at some mu in W dot lambda. Thus any strict submodule chain in M has length at most sum_{mu in W dot lambda} dim M_mu.

references.title: Etingof, §15.1 Lemma 15.9, p.81: finite weight-space detector method
Chen, Lecture 6 §2 Corollary 2.3 and Theorem 2.4 proof, pp.5–6: finite Weyl-orbit labels

items.proof_strategy: A singular vector gives a highest-weight cyclic submodule with scalar character equal to chi_lambda. Harish-Chandra identifies its highest label in the finite orbit. Weight-space exactness forces a positive detector increment at every strict chain step

items.title: Every object of O has finite length
items.statement: Every O-object admits a finite composition series and is both Noetherian and Artinian.
items.proof_strategy: Sum the finite detector bounds over central summands. Refine a chain until no refinement is possible; the bound forces finite termination and all factors are simple

items.title: Finite-dimensional Hom spaces in O
items.statement: Hom_O(M,N) is finite dimensional; End_O(L(lambda))=C.
items.proof_strategy: A map is determined by finitely many weight generators, whose images lie in finite-dimensional weight spaces; a simple highest-weight module has one-dimensional highest line

items.title: Restricted Chevalley dual
items.statement: For an h-semisimple module with finite-dimensional weight spaces define D(M)=direct sum M_mu^*, with (x f)(m)=f(tau(x)m) for the published Chevalley anti-involution.

items.title: Restricted self-duality of simple highest-weight modules
items.statement: D(L(lambda)) is isomorphic to L(lambda).
items.proof_strategy: On finite weight spaces annihilators turn a proper nonzero submodule of the dual into a proper nonzero submodule of L. Hence dual is simple. Its highest line has weight lambda, so the universal property identifies it with L(lambda)

items.title: Restricted duality is exact and involutive on O
items.statement: D is an exact contravariant equivalence O->O^op, with natural D^2=id and unchanged characters and composition multiplicities.

references.title: Chen, Lecture 8 §3 Lemma 3.8 and Theorem 3.9, p.5
Etingof, §20.4 Proposition 20.9, p.103; compare the different Cartan twist convention

items.proof_strategy: Dualize each finite weight space to prove exactness and biduality in the larger weight category. Dualize a finite composition series; its factors are the same simples. Qualified extension closure proves finite generation and membership in O without circularly assuming it

items.title: Standard and costandard objects
items.statement: Delta(lambda)=M(lambda); nabla(lambda)=D(M(lambda)).

items.title: The simple socle of a costandard object
items.statement: The unique simple submodule, and socle, of nabla(lambda) is L(lambda).
items.proof_strategy: Dualize the unique maximal Verma submodule; every simple submodule dualizes to the unique simple quotient

items.title: The integral Weyl group of a weight
items.statement: Phi_lambda={alpha: <lambda+rho,alpha^vee> in Z}; W_lambda is the subgroup generated by s_alpha for alpha in Phi_lambda. A linkage class is W_lambda dot lambda.

references.title: Humphreys, §3.4 definitions and invariance identities, p.52; §4.9, p.83 (reflection-generated convention)

items.title: Integral reflection linkage is an equivalence relation
items.statement: Phi_lambda is preserved by its root reflections. W_mu=W_lambda whenever mu in W_lambda dot lambda. The equivalence relation generated by integral reflection moves has classes W_lambda dot lambda.

references.title: §3.4 p.52, displayed definitions and invariance statements

items.proof_strategy: Pairing after reflection differs by an integral Cartan multiple of the integral pairing. This proves invariance under generators; reverse the reflection word for equivalence. Strong linkage stays in this class

items.title: Simple extensions cannot cross linkage classes
items.statement: A short exact sequence of two simple O-objects in distinct integral-reflection classes splits.

references.title: §1.13 pp.30–32 and §4.9 p.83, decomposed proof route

items.proof_strategy: Orient the extension by duality so quotient highest weight lambda is not strictly below submodule highest weight mu. Lift its highest vector as a weight vector; higher weights are absent, so it is singular. The generated highest-weight submodule either splits off or equals the nonsplit length-two extension. The latter makes L(mu) a Verma factor, forcing linkage

items.title: Splitting finite-length modules across separated simple classes
items.statement: A partition of simple O-labels with no nonsplit simple extensions across parts yields a unique functorial finite direct-sum decomposition of every O-object by composition-factor parts.
items.proof_strategy: Induct on kernel length via quotient pushouts, then quotient length via pullbacks and retractions; construct part summands by retractions and prove uniqueness by Hom vanishing

items.title: Central-character summands refine into linkage blocks
items.statement: The indecomposable categorical summands of O are the full subcategories with simple labels W_lambda dot lambda. Each lies in O_chi_lambda; a coarse central summand can have several linkage blocks.
items.proof_strategy: Use the splitting lemma for existence. For indecomposability, an integral reflection with nonzero pairing gives an embedding in one direction; the containing Verma is indecomposable by its unique highest line. Its two simple labels therefore belong to the same categorical summand. Iterate generators; zero pairing is a fixed point

items.title: Duality preserves linkage blocks and block orthogonality
items.statement: D preserves each linkage block. A Chevalley-contravariant bilinear form on an O-object pairs distinct block summands to zero.
items.proof_strategy: Duality preserves simple factors. A contravariant form induces a module map to the restricted dual because different weights are orthogonal. Hom between distinct block parts vanishes

items.title: Verma self-extensions in O split
items.statement: Every short exact sequence 0->M(lambda)->E->M(lambda)->0 in O splits.
items.proof_strategy: Lift the top vector as an actual weight vector; E has no weights above lambda, so the lift is singular and induces a section

items.title: Finite-dimensional tensoring preserves O
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional h-semisimple g-module E, M->E tensor M is exact and preserves O.
items.proof_strategy: Tensor basis of E with weight generators of M; induct on PBW degree using x(e tensor m)=xe tensor m+e tensor xm to establish finite generation. Support is a finite translate union; exactness holds over C

items.title: The Grothendieck group and character of O
items.statement: K0(O) is the free abelian group on isomorphism classes modulo short exact sequence relations; ch M=sum dim M_mu e^mu is supported in finitely many downward cones.

references.title: §2 Definition 2.4 and paragraph after Lemma 2.5, p.3

items.title: Simple and standard bases of K0(O)
items.statement: Classes of L(lambda), and separately M(lambda), form Z-bases of K0(O). In each finite central-character label set the transition matrix is unitriangular; the same holds for a downward-closed subset of that finite set.
items.proof_strategy: Jordan–Holder gives the simple basis and additive multiplicities. Restrict to the finite dot orbit, order by positive-root order; M(lambda) has top multiplicity one and other labels strictly lower. Invert a finite unitriangular integral matrix; take direct sum over central characters

title: Category O Finiteness Duality and Blocks — Examples

items.title: The regular integral sl2 block
items.statement: For n>=0, labels are n and -n-2; M(-n-2)=L(-n-2); 0->L(-n-2)->M(n)->L(n)->0 is nonsplit. The costandard reverses this sequence.

references.title: Chen, Lecture 2 §2 Example 2.16 and Exercise 2.17, p.4

items.proof_strategy: Verify using the sl2 PBW action, weight dimensions and duality; indecomposability proves nonsplitting

items.title: Nonintegral sl2 central characters split into two simple blocks
items.statement: For lambda not in Z, O_chi_lambda has two distinct singleton linkage blocks labelled lambda and -lambda-2; each is equivalent to finite-dimensional vector spaces.
items.proof_strategy: Use the dot-orbit central-character criterion and simple-object classification to identify exactly two labels; irreducibility and split self-extensions make each singleton block semisimple

items.title: A singular integral A2 central-character summand
items.statement: Take lambda=-omega1 in A2. lambda+rho=omega2 has stabilizer <s1>; its three dot-orbit labels are -omega1, -2omega2, -2omega1-omega2. They form one linkage block.
items.proof_strategy: In fundamental coordinates use s1(a,b)=(-a,a+b), s2(a,b)=(a+b,-b), subtract rho=(1,1); W_lambda=W. This is a labels/stabilizer calculation, not a claim about all composition multiplicities

items.title: The full algebraic Verma dual is too large
items.statement: For sl2 the full Chevalley-twisted dual of M(lambda) contains functionals with infinitely many nonzero weight components and is not h-semisimple.
items.proof_strategy: Choose f with f(f^n v)=1 for all n. No nonzero polynomial in h kills f because it would vanish at every distinct lambda-2n; hence f has infinite-dimensional h-orbit

items.title: Finite weight spaces and bounded support do not replace finite generation
items.statement: For sl2 the module direct sum_{n>=0} M(-2n) is h-semisimple and locally n+-finite, has support in -2Z>=0 and dim at weight -2k equal to k+1, but is not finitely generated.

references.title: Lecture 2 Definition 3.1; direct explicit hypothesis test

items.proof_strategy: Any finite set of vectors lies in finitely many direct summands, which form a proper submodule; count n=0,...,k for the weight dimension

items.title: Finite weight spaces alone do not give category O
items.statement: The lowest-weight sl2 Verma module of lowest weight 0 is cyclic and has one-dimensional spaces at 2n, n>=0, but has unbounded upward support and e acts freely; it is not in O.
items.proof_strategy: Construct induction from the negative Borel by the same PBW argument with e and f exchanged

items.title: An ambient extension can leave category O
items.statement: For sl2 induce the two-dimensional b-module with e=0, h v=lambda v, h w=lambda w+v. The induced module is an extension of M(lambda) by itself but is not h-semisimple.
items.proof_strategy: PBW freeness makes induction exact and preserves the nonzero Jordan pair in degree zero; therefore h-semisimplicity fails

items.title: O is not closed under arbitrary tensor products
items.statement: For sl2, M(0) tensor M(0) has finite weight spaces and downward support but is not finitely generated as a g-module, so not in O.
items.proof_strategy: Identify underlying space with C[x,y], with f multiplication by x+y. It is not finite over C[x+y], since quotient by x+y has infinite dimension. O-objects are finite over U(n-) by the finite induced flag lemma; derive contradiction
